A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TF/ETF research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, 20 tables and seven figures, support reliable comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments, Food101 end-to-end results, ablations, uncertainty evaluations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The TF/ETF networks, trust-discounting and fusion rules, losses, and training/testing algorithms are unchanged. New Appendix A explains existing opinion types without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Handwritten, Caltech101, PIE, Scene15, HMDB, CUB and image-text Food101, including the same noisy-input scenarios. Food101 was already present in v2 Section 4.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, Food101, robustness and timing comparisons. TEF is newly cited in related work but is not added to any reported evaluation.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, metrics, hyperparameters, ablation settings and Food101 encoders and optimizer remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol or revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: Both retain the TD, smoothing, view-selection and warm-up ablations, feature-similarity and conflict analyses, CUB uncertainty case study, and noisy-input tests. The corresponding analyses and plotted evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations over ten seeds for the main evaluations, three runs for Food101, and ten runs for timing. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical table entries and graphical results are unchanged. For example, ETF remains at 82.01±0.17 on Scene15 in Table 4 and 93.09±0.02 on Food101 in Table 9.

T1.justification: The equations, propositions and derivations are retained, with v2 Appendix B becoming v3 Appendix C. New Appendix A restates existing opinion representations rather than introducing new mathematics or assumptions.

C1.justification: V3's abstract explicitly frames the existing end-to-end experiment as a scalability evaluation, adding that emphasis to the contribution summary. The central trust-discounting, training, accuracy and consistency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 strengthens the expected uncertainty under conflict from 'not lower than' individual views to 'higher than' all views. The explanations of consistency and AUROC behavior, and the warm-up and training-time limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository address in the abstract; v2 only promised a future release. Hyperparameters and software/hardware details are unchanged. V3's appendix retains the future-release wording, and the PDFs cannot establish repository contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: V3 adds Liang et al. (2025), describing TEF's evolutionary fusion for improving pseudo-view quality. Other changes largely concern citation style and publication metadata for already-cited works; the research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the abstract, adds an opinion-explanation appendix, acknowledgments and an impact statement, and updates affiliations and citation style. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adopts ICML formatting, revises the title/author block, adds running headers, moves main-table captions above tables, and redistributes appendix displays, grouping Tables 15–20 together. Figure artwork and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit code location and explanation of functional versus referral opinions modestly improve accessibility and clarity, while the TEF citation updates context. Scientific evidence is unchanged. Editorial inconsistencies, including the retained future-release promise and the new 'Figure E.5' reference to Figure 4, temper these limited gains.
